choices.text: A copy of the text with spaces added around the string

prompt: In `Text("50 min").padding().background(.yellow).frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`, which wrapper is outermost?

choices.text: The text

prompt: Why does `.padding().background(.yellow)` show more yellow than `.background(.yellow).padding()`?
hint: A background is the size of what it wraps.

choices.text: In the first, the background wraps the padded text
choices.why: Right: it is as big as text plus padding.

choices.text: Padding paints yellow when it comes first
choices.why: Padding paints nothing in either order.

choices.text: The second background is drawn behind the screen
choices.why: It is drawn, just at the text's size.

choices.text: SwiftUI sorts modifiers, and backgrounds go last
choices.why: SwiftUI applies them in the order written.

prompt: According to Apple's documentation, what does a view with `.hidden()` do to the layout?

choices.text: Removes itself, so its siblings close the gap

prompt: What does a `ViewModifier`'s `body(content:)` receive as `content`?

prompt: When should a shared chain be a `ViewModifier` rather than a plain extension on `View`?
hint: Which of the two can hold state?

choices.text: Whenever it has more than three modifiers
choices.why: The length of the chain does not decide.

choices.text: When it is used on more than one screen
choices.why: Both forms are reusable on any number of screens.

choices.text: When it needs state of its own
choices.why: Right: a `ViewModifier` is a struct whose body may declare `@State`.

choices.text: When it should run off the main actor
choices.why: A `ViewModifier` is main-actor isolated by default, like a view.

choices.text: Because `.thinMaterial` cannot touch text

prompt: A `VStack` has `.font(.subheadline)`; its first `Text` has `.font(.headline)`. What font does each text get?

choices.text: All headline, since the first text sets it for the rest

choices.text: The first keeps its own; the rest inherit the stack's
choices.why: Right: the text's own font overrides the inherited one.

choices.text: The system font for all, since fonts do not inherit

choices.why: Fonts change sizes, but the inheritance rule is about containment.

choices.text: None; both are wrappers sized like their content
